text: Quick reminder before we add a safety net: plain CAST and CONVERT are all-or-nothing. If the conversion can't actually happen, SQL Server raises an error right there and the whole batch stops cold.

TRY_CAST attempts the exact same conversion, but instead of an error, a failure just comes back as NULL. Here, 'not a number' can't become an integer, so that one's NULL, while '123' converts fine and comes through as 123. The query keeps running either way.

TRY_CONVERT is the same idea applied to CONVERT, with the same signature you already know, including the optional style number. Valid date text converts normally; invalid text just comes back NULL instead of killing the batch.

Here's where this earns its place in a real pipeline. PersonPhone stores numbers with dashes and parentheses mixed in. Strip those out and try TRY_CAST to BIGINT, and whatever still fails to convert -- an extension, stray letters, odd formatting -- shows up as NULL, which you can filter on directly.

That's the whole point of TRY_CAST and TRY_CONVERT: validate or clean data by letting bad values surface as NULL, instead of letting one bad row take down the entire batch. Next up, STRING_AGG -- concatenating many rows of text into one single string.
